recipes.title: Chive Cheese Mold
recipes.source_note: Cottage Cheese Recipe Book - Appetizers, Salads, Salad Dressings, Breads, Main Dishes, Desserts (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Dissolve flavored gelatin in hot water. Add cold water. Chill until syrupy. Mash avocado; mix with cottage cheese, mayonnaise, and nut meats, and add to thickened gelatin. Pour into mold and chill. Garnish with orange slices or segments. Serves 6.

recipes.title: Molasses Ice Cream
recipes.source_note: Grandma's Recipes for Mother and Daughter (Project Gutenberg, public domain)
recipes.description: Vintage recipe

instructions.text: Turn refrigerator control to coldest point. Set out ice tray. Crush rennet tablet; dissolve in cold water. Mix cream, sugar, and molasses; warm over low heat to 110° F. (lukewarm), stirring constantly. Add vanilla and dissolved rennet tablet. Pour, at once, into ice tray. Do not move until set (about 10 minutes). Freeze in ice cube unit of refrigerator until almost stiff. Turn into a bowl. Beat until smooth. Return to ice tray. Freeze until stiff (3 to 4 hours).
Molasses Coffee Ice Cream: Add ¼ cup cold, double-strength coffee.

recipes.title: Ricotta Cheese
recipes.description: A simple heat and acid precipitated cheese that can be made from whole or skim milk. Light, creamy, and versatile.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 190-195°F (88-91°C). Stir gently and heat slowly. Optional: Add 1 tsp salt to milk before heating.
When milk reaches temperature, add citric acid or vinegar and stir gently. The curds will begin to separate from the whey.
As curds rise, use a perforated ladle to gently move the curd from the sides of the pot to the center.
Let sit for 10-15 minutes, then ladle curds into a colander lined with butter muslin or cheesecloth.
Drain for 20-30 minutes for a moist ricotta, longer for a drier texture. Refrigerate and use within 1 week.

recipes.title: Queso Fresco
recipes.description: A fresh Mexican cheese made with rennet. Crumbly texture, mild flavor. Melts when heated unlike Queso Blanco.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add starter culture and stir for 3 minutes.
Add diluted rennet and stir gently for 30 seconds. Let set for 30-45 minutes until you get a clean break.
Cut the curd into 1/4 inch pieces.
Raise temperature to 95°F (35°C) over 20 minutes, stirring gently every few minutes.
Let curds settle for 5 minutes, then drain whey.
Mix in cheese salt thoroughly.
Transfer curds to cheese mold and press at 35 lbs pressure for 6 hours.
Remove from mold, refrigerate, and enjoy within 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Chèvre (Fresh Goat Cheese)
recipes.description: A tangy, creamy fresh goat cheese. Easy to make at home with just goat milk and culture.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb from 1 gallon goat milk

instructions.text: Bring goat milk to room temperature (68-72°F / 20-22°C).
Sprinkle culture over milk surface. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, then stir in.
Add diluted rennet if using and stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and set aside at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
The curd will show a thin layer of whey on top and may crack slightly when ready.
Gently ladle curds into cheese molds or a colander lined with butter muslin.
Drain for 6-12 hours. Less time for moister, sweeter cheese; more time for drier, tangier cheese.
Add salt to taste. Roll in herbs, ash, or spices if desired. Refrigerate up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Feta Cheese
recipes.description: A tangy, salty brine-cured cheese traditionally made from sheep or goat milk. Can also be made with cow milk.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add starter culture and lipase. Stir gently, then let ripen for 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet and stir for 30 seconds. Let set for 45-50 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Stir curds gently for 20-30 minutes while maintaining temperature.
Drain whey and transfer curds to cheese mold. Press lightly for 4-6 hours, flipping every hour.
Remove from mold and cut into blocks. Salt all surfaces and let drain for 2-3 days, turning daily.
Prepare brine (1/2 lb salt per gallon water). Submerge feta and age in refrigerator for 30+ days.

recipes.title: Halloumi
recipes.description: A Cypriot cheese with a high melting point, perfect for grilling or frying. Squeaky texture when fresh.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add diluted rennet and stir for 30 seconds.
Let set for 45-60 minutes until a firm curd forms with clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey (save it!) and transfer curds to mold. Press at 20 lbs for 1 hour.
Cut pressed cheese into blocks. Heat reserved whey to 190-195°F (88-91°C).
Place cheese blocks in hot whey for 30-40 minutes until they float.
Remove, drain, and sprinkle with salt and mint while warm. Fold if desired.
Cool and refrigerate. Store in light brine for longer keeping.

recipes.title: 30-Minute Mozzarella
recipes.description: A quick version of fresh mozzarella using citric acid for fast curd formation. Stretchy and delicious.

instructions.text: Pour citric acid solution into a large pot. Add cold milk and stir well.
Heat milk slowly to 90°F (32°C), stirring gently.
Remove from heat. Add diluted rennet and stir for 30 seconds. Cover and let sit 5 minutes.
Check for clean break. Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Return to heat and warm curds to 105°F (40°C) while stirring gently.
Remove curds with slotted spoon and drain whey. Microwave for 1 minute.
Drain off whey, add salt, and knead. Microwave 30 seconds more.
Knead and stretch until smooth and shiny. Shape into balls.
Place in ice water to set shape. Use fresh or refrigerate up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Farmer's Cheese
recipes.description: A simple fresh cheese similar to cottage cheese but pressed. Mild flavor, versatile for sweet or savory dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Stir in buttermilk.
Add diluted rennet and stir for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at 86°F for 1 hour until firm curd forms.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes.
Slowly heat to 110°F (43°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Add salt and mix well. Gather cloth and press under weight for 1-2 hours.
Refrigerate and use within 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Basket Cheese
recipes.attribution: Rosanne Coreano, NY (via New England Cheesemaking Supply Co.)
recipes.source_note: cheesemaking.com - traditional recipe handed down by word of mouth
recipes.description: A mild Italian-American cheese traditionally shaped in a basket. Delicious on bruschetta with olive oil and tomato.

instructions.text: Heat milk to lukewarm (86-90°F / 30-32°C).
Add diluted rennet and stir gently. Turn off heat.
Let set for about 40 minutes until firm curd forms.
Turn heat back on low for about 2 minutes.
Using a slotted spoon, pull the curds to the side of the pot. Keep moving curds for about 10 minutes to break them up and help them drain.
Remove curds with slotted spoon and place into a basket or cheese mold.
Return basket to the pot, submerging in whey. Press curds into basket with hands.
Remove basket from whey. Place a smaller mold inside with 6-8 oz weight on top. Press for 2 hours.
Turn cheese over, salt to taste, and continue pressing for 1.5 hours more.
Serve drizzled with olive oil, garlic salt, and fresh tomato slices.

recipes.title: Farmhouse Cheddar
recipes.description: A classic aged cheddar with a gentle, mild flavor. Uses the traditional cheddaring technique for authentic texture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C) using a water bath for stable temperature.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk. Add starter culture, let rehydrate 2 minutes, stir in. Ripen for 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir for 30 seconds. Let set for 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 102°F for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Curds should be firm.
Drain whey. Cut curd mass into slabs. Stack and flip slabs every 15 minutes for 2 hours (cheddaring).
Mill curds into thumb-sized pieces. Add salt and mix well.
Pack into mold and press at 10 lbs for 15 min, then 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms. Wax or vacuum seal. Age at 55°F for 4-12 weeks.

recipes.title: Gouda Cheese
recipes.description: A Dutch semi-hard cheese with a creamy, slightly sweet flavor. Uses washed curd technique.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add C101 culture package. Let ripen for 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir for 30 seconds. Let set 40 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of the whey. Add 140°F water slowly to raise temperature to 100°F over 15 minutes (washed curd).
Stir curds for 20 minutes at 100°F.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to mold and press at 10 lbs for 30 min, then 20 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Prepare brine (1 lb salt per gallon water). Brine cheese for 3 hours per pound.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

recipes.title: Brie Cheese
recipes.description: A soft-ripened French cheese with a creamy interior and white bloomy rind.

instructions.text: Heat milk and cream to 90°F (32°C).
Add cultures (mesophilic, P. candidum, G. candidum). Let rehydrate 2 minutes, stir in. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently. Let set for 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1 inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds. Let drain at room temperature, flipping every 2-3 hours.
After 24 hours, unmold and salt all surfaces.
Place on ripening mat. Age at 55°F and 90% humidity for 4-6 weeks.
White mold will develop in 10-14 days. Flip daily. Ripe when interior is soft and creamy.

recipes.title: Camembert Cheese
recipes.description: A rich, creamy French cheese with a bloomy white rind. Smaller and more intense than Brie.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C).
Add cultures. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, stir in. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Camembert molds. Let drain 24 hours, flipping every few hours.
Unmold and salt all surfaces lightly.
Age at 55°F with 90% humidity for 3-5 weeks.
White mold appears in 7-10 days. Cheese is ripe when soft throughout.

recipes.title: Stilton Blue Cheese
recipes.description: The 'King of English Cheeses' - a rich, creamy blue with complex flavor. Requires careful aging.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add cultures. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 1 hour for firm curd.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir for 30 minutes at 86°F.
Drain whey. Loosely pack curds into mold. Turn frequently for first hour, then 2x daily for 3 days.
Keep at 70°F for 3-5 days. Remove from mold and wrap in cloth for 5 more days.
At 5 weeks, pierce with 1/8 inch needle (1 hole per inch) through top and bottom.
Age at 55°F with 95% humidity. Ready at 12 weeks minimum.

recipes.title: Colby Cheese
recipes.description: A semi-hard American cheese with mild, sweet flavor and open texture. Uses washed curd technique.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add starter culture, ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 3/8 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain most of the whey. Add cool water (60°F) to lower temperature to 80°F (washed curd). Stir 15 minutes.
Drain water. Add salt and mix well.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 4-6 weeks.

recipes.title: Pepper Jack Cheese
recipes.description: A spicy variation of Monterey Jack with added peppercorns or jalapeños.

instructions.text: Toast peppercorns in dry pan until they pop. Crack lightly with mortar and pestle.
Heat milk to 88°F (31°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add starter culture, ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Add peppers and salt, mix thoroughly.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 1-4 months.

recipes.title: Havarti Cheese
recipes.description: A Danish semi-soft cheese with a creamy, buttery flavor and small irregular holes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C) in a water bath.
Add C101 culture. Ripen for 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently for 1 minute. Let set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Add hot water (130°F) equal to 15-25% of milk volume over 10 minutes. Target 95-100°F.
Add salt and stir curds for 15-30 minutes.
Drain curds. Pack into cloth-lined mold.
Press at 8 lbs for 15-20 min, then 16 lbs for 2 hours. Turn every 30 minutes.
Brine for 2 hours per pound.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-3 months.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese
recipes.description: A fresh, mild cheese with small curds. Can be made with small or large curds.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter culture. Stir well.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently.
Cover and let set at 72°F for 5-8 hours until curd forms.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes (small curd) or 1 inch cubes (large curd).
Very slowly heat to 110°F (43°C) over 30-40 minutes. Stir gently.
Hold at 110°F for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain through cheesecloth. Rinse curds with cold water.
Add salt. For creamed cottage cheese, stir in heavy cream.
Refrigerate. Use within 1-2 weeks.

recipes.title: Cream Cheese
recipes.description: A rich, spreadable fresh cheese perfect for bagels or baking.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb from 1/2 gallon milk + 1 pint cream

instructions.text: Mix milk and cream. Heat to 86°F (30°C).
Add calcium chloride, then starter culture. Stir well.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently.
Cover and let set at room temperature (68-72°F) for 12-24 hours.
When curd is thick and pulls away from sides, it's ready.
Line colander with butter muslin. Pour in curds.
Drain 12-24 hours in refrigerator until desired thickness.
Add salt and mix well. Store refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Quark
recipes.description: A German fresh cheese, milder than yogurt. High protein, low fat. Great for baking or eating plain.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add culture. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, stir in.
Add rennet drops if using. Stir gently.
Cover and let set 12-24 hours. Temperature can drop to 68-71°F.
Curd is ready when it has a yogurt-like consistency.
Pour into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Drain 4-8 hours until desired consistency.
For smoother texture, blend or whip. Add cream for richer quark.
Refrigerate. Use within 7-10 days.

recipes.title: Baby Swiss Cheese
recipes.description: A mild, nutty cheese with small eyes (holes). Easier version of traditional Swiss Emmentaler.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C).
Add cultures (thermophilic and propionic). Ripen 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 120°F (49°C) over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes. Curds should be firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, then 25 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine for 12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Age at 55°F for 2 weeks, then at 68°F for 2-3 weeks for eye development.
Return to 55°F for 1-2 more months. Eyes should form during warm phase.

recipes.title: Gruyère Cheese
recipes.description: A classic Alpine cheese with rich, complex flavor. Minimal or no holes. Excellent for fondue.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C).
Add all cultures. Ripen 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd to rice-grain size (very small).
Slowly raise temperature to 122°F (50°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 122°F for 45 minutes. Curds should be very firm.
Drain whey. Pack into large mold. Press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 24 hours.
Brine for 24 hours.
Age at 55°F, washing rind with brine weekly for first month.
Continue aging 8-14 months minimum for full flavor development.

recipes.title: Provolone Cheese
recipes.description: An Italian pasta filata (stretched curd) cheese. Can be mild or aged for sharper flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add lipase if using.
Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes.
Slowly raise to 118°F (48°C) over 30 minutes, stirring.
Let curds mat together at bottom of pot. Drain whey.
Let curd mass ripen 2-4 hours until it stretches smoothly in hot water (170°F).
Cut curd into strips. Stretch and knead in hot water until smooth.
Shape into desired form (pear, sausage, etc.). Cool in ice water.
Brine for 6-12 hours. Hang to dry. Age at 55°F for 2-12 months.

recipes.title: Asiago Cheese
recipes.description: An Italian cheese that can be fresh (Asiago Pressato) or aged (Asiago d'Allevo). Nutty, slightly sweet.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95-97°F (35-36°C).
Add cultures. This is a small amount for slow acid development. Ripen 20 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 40-50 minutes.
Cut curd to rice-grain size.
Slowly raise to 118°F (48°C) over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 118°F for 30 minutes.
Drain whey. Pack into mold. Press at 15 lbs, increasing to 40 lbs over 12 hours.
Brine for 12 hours.
Age at 55°F. Fresh Asiago: 1-2 months. Aged Asiago: 6-12 months.

recipes.title: Traditional Feta (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: Authentic Greek PDO feta requires at least 70% sheep's milk
recipes.description: Authentic Greek feta made primarily from sheep's milk, as protected by EU designation. Tangy, crumbly, and brined.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk (and goat's milk if using) to 86°F (30°C).
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk. Stir well.
Dissolve lipase in 1/4 cup cool water. Add to milk and stir.
Sprinkle starter culture over surface. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, then stir. Ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently for 30 seconds. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir curds for 20 minutes while maintaining 86°F. Curds will firm up.
Line a colander with cheesecloth. Drain curds.
Transfer to feta molds or form into blocks. Let drain at room temperature 24 hours, turning every few hours.
Cut into blocks and salt all surfaces generously. Let drain 2-3 more days, turning and re-salting daily.
Prepare brine: dissolve 1/2 lb salt per gallon of water. Add a splash of whey.
Submerge feta in brine. Age in refrigerator for minimum 30 days (60+ days for fuller flavor).

notes: True Greek feta PDO requires minimum 70% sheep's milk, remainder goat's milk
Sheep's milk has higher fat content than cow's milk, creating richer feta
The longer it ages in brine, the tangier and firmer it becomes

recipes.title: Pecorino Romano (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Italian hard cheese, made exclusively from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A hard, salty Italian cheese made from sheep's milk. Sharp and piquant, essential for pasta dishes like cacio e pepe.
recipes.servings_yield: About 3-4 lbs from 4 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 100°F (38°C) - slightly warmer than many cheeses due to sheep milk's composition.
Add thermophilic culture. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Dissolve lamb rennet paste in warm water (or use liquid rennet). Add to milk, stir 30 seconds.
Let set 20-30 minutes until firm curd forms.
Cut curd into rice-grain sized pieces (very small for this hard cheese).
Slowly raise temperature to 118°F (48°C) over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring at 118°F for 45 minutes until curds are very firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into large mold. Press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 24 hours.
Remove from mold. Rub all surfaces with salt. Place on aging board.
Salt rub daily for first week, then weekly for first month.
Age at 55°F with 85% humidity. Turn weekly.
Minimum aging: 5 months for table cheese, 8-12 months for grating cheese.

notes: Lamb rennet paste gives traditional sharp, piquant flavor
'Pecora' means sheep in Italian - this cheese can only be made from sheep's milk
The longer it ages, the harder and more intense the flavor

missing_inputs: for rubbing and brine cheese salt

recipes.title: Manchego-Style Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.attribution: Based on traditional La Mancha methods
recipes.source_note: True Manchego is made only from Manchega sheep milk in La Mancha, Spain
recipes.description: A firm, buttery Spanish cheese with a distinctive herringbone rind pattern. Nutty and slightly tangy.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2-3 lbs from 3 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: Manchega breed preferred, or any sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add mesophilic culture. Let ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Continue stirring at 104°F for 30 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into Manchego mold (with traditional zigzag pattern).
Press at 10 lbs for 1 hour, then 25 lbs for 6-12 hours.
Remove from mold. Brine for 12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms.
Age at 55°F with 85% humidity. Can rub with olive oil for traditional finish.
Fresco: 2 weeks. Semi-curado: 3-6 months. Curado: 6-12 months. Viejo: 12+ months.

notes: The zigzag rind pattern comes from traditional esparto grass molds
True DO Manchego comes only from Manchega sheep in La Mancha region
Sheep's milk gives Manchego its distinctive rich, lanolin-y undertone

recipes.title: Roquefort-Style Blue Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: True Roquefort is made from raw Lacaune sheep milk and aged in caves near Roquefort-sur-Soulzon, France
recipes.description: A tangy, creamy blue cheese made from sheep's milk. Rich and complex with distinctive blue-green veining.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2-3 lbs from 3 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 90 minutes for a moist curd.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Handle very gently to preserve moisture.
Let curds rest in whey 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Gently ladle curds into tall cylindrical mold without pressing.
Let drain at room temperature 24-48 hours, turning every few hours.
Remove from mold. Salt all surfaces. Let drain 2 more days.
Pierce cheese with sterilized needle from top and bottom (holes about 1 inch apart) to allow air entry for blue mold development.
Age at 50°F with 95% humidity. The high humidity is crucial.
Blue veining should develop within 30-60 days.
Wrap in foil when veining is established. Continue aging 3-6 months total.

notes: True Roquefort must be made from raw milk of Lacaune sheep
The caves of Roquefort have natural Penicillium roqueforti
High humidity and cool temperatures are essential for proper mold development
Sheep's milk gives Roquefort its distinctive rich, tangy character

recipes.title: Ricotta Salata (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: A pressed, salted, aged ricotta made from sheep's milk whey
recipes.description: A firm, salted ricotta that can be sliced or grated. Milky and slightly tangy - traditional Sicilian cheese.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb from whey of 3 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: leftover from making other sheep's milk cheese
dissolved in 2 tbsp water, or use lemon juice

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk whey to 185-195°F (85-90°C). Add the cup of fresh milk if using.
When temperature is reached, add citric acid solution and stir gently.
Small curds will form and rise to the surface. Remove from heat.
Let rest 10 minutes, then skim curds into a ricotta mold or cheesecloth-lined colander.
Drain 2-3 hours until curds hold together.
Mix salt thoroughly into the curds.
Pack into a small cheese mold. Press at 5 lbs for 12 hours.
Remove from mold. Place on a drying mat.
Age at 55°F with 75% humidity for 3-4 weeks minimum.
Turn daily for first week, then every few days.
The cheese will develop a thin rind and firm texture suitable for slicing or grating.

notes: The sheep's milk whey gives it a richer, more complex flavor than cow's milk ricotta
Can be grated over pasta like Pecorino, or sliced for salads

recipes.title: Kasseri Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: A semi-hard pasta filata cheese made from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A Greek stretched-curd cheese similar to provolone but made from sheep's milk. Tangy and slightly sharp.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 90°F (32°C). Add calcium chloride and lipase if using.
Add thermophilic culture. Let ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain most of the whey. Let curds mat together.
Let curd mass acidify for 2-4 hours until it stretches smoothly in 170°F water.
Cut curd into strips. Stretch and knead in hot water (170°F) until smooth and shiny.
Form into a ball or loaf shape. Cool in cold water.
Brine for 8-12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Air dry until rind forms, about 1-2 days.
Age at 55°F for 2-4 months. Can be waxed after rind forms.

notes: Kasseri is a 'pasta filata' (stretched curd) cheese like mozzarella and provolone
The sheep's milk gives it a richer, tangier flavor than cow's milk versions

recipes.title: Oscypek-Style Smoked Sheep Cheese
recipes.source_note: Traditional Polish smoked cheese from the Tatra Mountains, made from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A smoked sheep's milk cheese with a decorative spindle shape. Slightly salty with a rich smoky flavor.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1.5 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: can blend with up to 40% cow's milk traditionally

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter culture. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curd into small pieces. Stir gently.
Slowly raise temperature to 95°F (35°C) over 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Work curds by hand, kneading and squeezing out moisture.
Add salt and knead into the curd mass.
Shape into traditional spindle form (pointed at both ends) or decorative molds.
Press by hand to create decorative patterns on surface.
Let dry at room temperature for 24 hours.
Cold smoke at 70-90°F (21-32°C) for 6-12 hours until golden brown.
Age 2-3 weeks or enjoy fresh after smoking.

notes: True Oscypek has EU Protected Designation of Origin
Traditionally made in wooden molds with carved decorative patterns
The smoking gives it a beautiful golden-brown rind
Slice and grill on a hot pan until slightly melted

recipes.title: Cultured Sheep's Milk Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Authentic cultured cream cheese method using sheep's milk
recipes.description: Authentic cultured cream cheese using sheep's milk and mesophilic starter for complex flavor development. This method produces the most authentic cream cheese taste.

instructions.text: Combine sheep's milk and cream in a pot. Warm gently to 75°F (24°C).
Sprinkle mesophilic starter over surface. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, then stir gently to incorporate.
Add diluted rennet and stir gently with an up-and-down motion for 30 seconds.
Cover and let culture at room temperature (70-75°F) for 12-14 hours or overnight until set like yogurt.
The curd is ready when it pulls away cleanly from the sides and whey pools on top.
Line a colander with butter muslin. Gently ladle curds into the muslin without breaking them up too much.
Tie corners of muslin and hang to drain at room temperature for 6-8 hours, or refrigerate overnight.
When cheese reaches desired consistency (thick but still spreadable), transfer to a bowl.
Add salt and mix well. For extra smooth texture, blend briefly in food processor.
Pack into containers and refrigerate. Best after chilling for several hours.

notes: The cultured method develops more complex, tangy flavors than acid-set
Use only 2 drops of rennet - too much creates a rubbery texture
Sheep's milk cream cheese will be yellower than cow's milk version
Can be flavored with herbs, garlic, honey, or fruit after draining

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Ricotta
recipes.source_note: Ricotta means 're-cooked' - traditionally made from whey
recipes.description: Fresh, creamy ricotta from sheep's milk. Richer and sweeter than cow's milk ricotta with a delicate, slightly nutty flavor.

instructions.text: Pour sheep's milk and cream into a heavy pot. Add salt.
Heat slowly over medium heat to 185-190°F (85-88°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice and stir gently once.
Let sit undisturbed 10-15 minutes until curds form.
Line a colander with cheesecloth. Gently ladle curds into cloth.
Drain 1-2 hours for creamy ricotta, longer for drier texture.
Transfer to container. Refrigerate up to 1 week.

notes: Sheep's milk ricotta is naturally sweeter and richer
Use within a week for best flavor
Perfect for lasagna, cannoli, or eating fresh with honey

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cottage Cheese
recipes.description: Creamy cottage cheese made from sheep's milk with small, tender curds. Higher in protein and fat than cow's milk version.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 72°F (22°C). Add starter, stir, let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently. Cover and let set 4-6 hours until firm.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Slowly heat to 110°F (43°C) over 30-40 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 110°F for 20-30 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain through cheesecloth. Rinse curds with cold water.
Toss curds with salt and cream. Refrigerate.

notes: Small curd develops at lower cooking temps, large curd at higher
Add herbs or fruit for variations

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Quark
recipes.source_note: Traditional quark adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Smooth, tangy fresh cheese similar to Greek yogurt but milder. Sheep's milk adds richness and depth.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter, stir. Add diluted rennet, stir briefly.
Cover and let culture 12-18 hours at room temp until set like yogurt.
Ladle into cheesecloth-lined strainer.
Drain 6-12 hours until desired thickness.
Blend smooth if desired. Season with salt to taste.

notes: Use for baking, spreads, or eating plain
Can substitute for sour cream or cream cheese in recipes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Mozzarella
recipes.source_note: Traditional mozzarella adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Fresh stretched-curd mozzarella from sheep's milk. Creamier and richer than cow's milk version with excellent melt.

instructions.text: Add citric acid solution to cold milk. Heat to 90°F (32°C), stirring.
Remove from heat. Add rennet, stir gently 30 seconds. Cover, let set 5-10 min.
Check for clean break. Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Heat curds to 105°F (40°C), stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press curds together in pot.
Heat water or whey to 170°F (77°C). Submerge curd until pliable.
Stretch and fold curd until smooth and shiny. Add salt while stretching.
Form into balls. Cool in ice water bath.

notes: Sheep milk mozzarella has higher fat for better melt
Use same day for best texture
Store in whey or salted water up to 1 week

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Provolone
recipes.source_note: Traditional provolone adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Aged stretched-curd cheese with sharp, tangy flavor. Sheep's milk adds complexity and richness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 97°F (36°C). Add lipase dissolved in water. Stir.
Add starter, let ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Stir gently, heat to 118°F (48°C).
Drain whey. Let curd mat and acidify until pH 5.2 (stretches in hot water).
Stretch in 170°F water until smooth. Form into traditional shapes.
Brine 12 hours per pound.
Hang to dry. Age 2-12 months in cool cave or fridge.

notes: Can be smoked for additional flavor

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Scamorza
recipes.description: Pear-shaped stretched cheese, often smoked. Firmer than mozzarella with concentrated flavor.

instructions.text: Make mozzarella curd using standard method.
Stretch until very smooth and elastic.
Form into pear shape with pinched 'neck' at top.
Tie string around neck for hanging.
Hang to dry 1-2 weeks in cool area.
Optional: cold smoke for Scamorza Affumicata.

notes: Great melting cheese for pizza and pasta

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Caciocavallo
recipes.source_note: Traditional caciocavallo adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Gourd-shaped aged pasta filata cheese. Name means 'cheese on horseback' from traditional drying method.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 40 minutes.
Cut curd small (1/4 inch). Cook to 118°F.
Drain and let curd acidify 3-5 hours until stretchy.
Stretch in hot water. Form into gourd shape with small ball on top.
Tie with raffia at neck. Hang in pairs over rod.
Brine 8-12 hours. Dry and age 3-6 months.

notes: Traditional shape resembles a teardrop with a topknot
Aged versions develop sharp, tangy flavor
Young versions are mild and great for grilling

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gouda
recipes.source_note: Traditional Gouda adapted for sheep's milk (like Ewephoria)
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty washed-curd cheese. Sheep's milk version has caramel notes and rich, buttery texture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride if using.
Add starter, ripen 10 minutes. Add rennet, set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with 90°F water (washing step).
Slowly heat to 100°F over 30 minutes while stirring.
Drain whey. Press curds into mold at 10 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs.
Brine 12 hours. Air dry 2-3 days.
Wax or vacuum seal. Age 2-12 months.

notes: Washing the curd removes lactose, creating sweeter cheese
Aged Gouda (12+ months): crystalline, caramel notes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Edam
recipes.source_note: Traditional Edam adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, slightly nutty semi-hard cheese in distinctive ball shape. Lower fat than Gouda.

instructions.text: Partially skim cream from milk. Heat to 86°F.
Add starter, ripen 30 minutes. Add rennet, set 45 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Remove 1/3 whey, replace with warm water.
Heat to 100°F. Stir 30 minutes.
Press into round mold. Press 3-6 hours.
Brine 8 hours. Dry and wax with red wax.
Age 1-4 months.

notes: Milder than Gouda due to lower fat

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Traditional cheddar method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Sharp, crumbly cheddar made with sheep's milk. Richer and more complex than cow's milk cheddar.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride and starter. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Cut curd mass into slabs.
Stack and flip slabs every 15 minutes for 2 hours (cheddaring).
Mill curd into finger-sized pieces. Mix in salt.
Press at 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 3-5 days until dry to touch. Wax or bandage.
Age 3-24 months at 55°F.

notes: Sheep milk cheddar develops complex, nutty notes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Colby
recipes.source_note: Wisconsin Colby adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, moist American cheese with open texture. Sheep's milk adds subtle sweetness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add annatto if using for orange color.
Add starter, ripen 45 minutes. Add rennet, set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 3/8-inch cubes.
Heat to 102°F over 30 minutes.
Drain whey to curd level. Add cold water to 80°F.
Stir 15 minutes. Drain. Add salt.
Press lightly at 20 lbs for 20 minutes, then 40 lbs for 3 hours.
Air dry, wax, age 1-3 months.

notes: Best at 1-2 months - doesn't improve with long aging

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Brie
recipes.source_note: Traditional Brie adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Creamy, bloomy-rind cheese with buttery interior. Sheep's milk creates an exceptionally rich, complex Brie.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride, starter, and P. candidum. Stir.
Ripen 90 minutes. Add rennet, let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds. Do not press.
Flip every few hours for 24 hours as whey drains.
Salt all surfaces. Air dry 2-3 days at 50-55°F.
Age at 50-55°F, 95% humidity for 4-6 weeks until white bloom covers surface.
Wrap and refrigerate. Best at room temperature.

notes: High humidity is crucial for proper bloom development
Sheep's milk Brie will be yellower than cow's milk version
Ripe when soft throughout with slight ammonia aroma

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Camembert
recipes.source_note: Traditional Camembert adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Smaller, more intense cousin of Brie with earthy, mushroomy notes. Sheep's milk adds depth.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, P. candidum, and Geotrichum. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir 20 minutes. Ladle into Camembert molds.
Flip every 2 hours for 12 hours, then twice daily.
Unmold after 2 days. Salt surfaces.
Age at 50-55°F, high humidity, for 3-5 weeks.
Wrap when fully bloomed. Enjoy at room temp.

notes: Smaller size means faster ripening than Brie
Should be gooey when fully ripe
Traditional Camembert de Normandie uses raw milk

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Coulommiers
recipes.description: The predecessor to Brie, smaller and thicker with more intense flavor. Sheep's milk version is exceptional.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and mold. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet, set 90 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 3/4-inch cubes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Ladle into tall Coulommiers molds.
Flip regularly for 24 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Dry 2 days.
Age 3-4 weeks at 52°F with high humidity.

notes: Thicker than Brie, so center ripens more slowly
Original Brie-style cheese from Île-de-France region

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gorgonzola-Style
recipes.source_note: Gorgonzola method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Creamy Italian blue with sheep's milk richness. Develops sweet, spicy, earthy notes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Let set 1 hour until firm.
Cut into 1-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir 30 minutes without heating.
Drain whey. Ladle curds into tall mold without pressing.
Flip several times daily for 3-4 days.
Salt all surfaces. Pierce with needle to create air channels.
Age 3-6 months at 46-50°F, 95% humidity. Pierce again at 1 month.

notes: Piccante version: aged longer, more intense
Piercing allows oxygen in for blue mold growth

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Stilton-Style
recipes.source_note: Stilton method adapted for sheep's milk (like Lanark Blue)
recipes.description: King of English blues made with sheep's milk. Rich, creamy with bold blue veining.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and blue mold. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let settle 10 min.
Drain whey. Let curds mat and acidify 1-2 hours.
Mill curds. Mix with salt.
Pack loosely into tall cylindrical mold. Do not press.
Flip twice daily for 5 days. Smooth sides with knife.
Pierce all over at 6 weeks. Age 3-4 months at 50°F.

notes: True Stilton is PDO protected - this is 'Stilton-style'
Lanark Blue is a Scottish sheep's milk blue similar to this
Rubbing rind helps develop the characteristic crust

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Danish Blue Style
recipes.source_note: Danish Blue adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Sharp, salty blue cheese. Sheep's milk adds creaminess to the bold flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add lipase, starter, blue mold. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Stir gently 15 minutes.
Drain whey. Pack curds loosely in mold.
Flip twice daily for 3 days.
Salt heavily. Pierce all surfaces.
Age 2-3 months at 50°F, high humidity.

notes: Very salty - use less if preferred

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Havarti
recipes.source_note: Traditional Havarti adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Buttery, flexible cheese with small irregular holes. Sheep's milk makes it extra creamy.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Let rest 10 min. Remove 1/3 whey, replace with warm water.
Heat slowly to 100°F over 30 minutes.
Drain. Press lightly at 8 lbs for 30 min, flip, 15 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine 12 hours. Dry and wax.
Age 2-3 months at 50°F.

notes: Can add dill, caraway, or jalapeño for flavored versions
Light pressing creates characteristic small holes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Fontina
recipes.source_note: Fontina Val d'Aosta adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Nutty, earthy semi-soft cheese from the Alps. Sheep's milk adds depth and richness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 35-40 minutes.
Cut into 1/4-inch cubes.
Heat to 118°F over 45 minutes, stirring.
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, 25 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine 12 hours. Dry.
Age 3-4 months, washing rind with brine weekly.

notes: True Fontina is a washed-rind cheese
Develops earthy, mushroomy notes with age

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gruyère-Style
recipes.source_note: Gruyère method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Complex, nutty Alpine cheese. Sheep's milk creates intense, sweet-savory flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 15 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces.
Heat to 120°F over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 12 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Age 6-12 months at 55°F, washing with brine weekly.

notes: High cooking temp creates signature dense texture

recipes.title: Idiazabal (Basque Smoked Sheep Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Basque sheep cheese, often smoked
recipes.description: Firm, buttery Basque cheese traditionally made from Latxa sheep milk. Often lightly smoked with cherry or beech wood.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into small pieces (lentil-sized).
Heat to 104°F while stirring gently.
Drain and press firmly at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Air dry 1 week. Optional: cold smoke 12-24 hours.
Age 2-5 months at 50°F.

notes: Smoked version (ahumado) uses cherry or beech wood
Unsmoked version shows purer sheep milk flavor
PDO requires milk from Latxa or Carranzana sheep

recipes.title: Roncal (Navarre Sheep Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional cheese from Roncal Valley, Navarre
recipes.description: Hard, granular sheep cheese with intense, piquant flavor. Spain's first protected designation cheese (1981).

instructions.text: Heat raw milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd very small (rice grain size).
Heat to 104°F, stirring constantly.
Press curds by hand in mold, then press at 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Rub surface with salt over several days.
Age minimum 4 months, up to 8 for fuller flavor.

notes: PDO requires raw sheep milk from Rasa and Lacha breeds
Develops sharp, slightly spicy flavor with age
Rind should be rubbed with olive oil during aging

recipes.title: Torta del Casar (Extremadura Soft Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Unique soft cheese coagulated with thistle
recipes.description: Creamy, oozing cheese with bitter, herbaceous notes from cardoon thistle rennet. Cut top off and scoop like fondue.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 82-86°F.
Add cardoon thistle extract. Let set 60-90 minutes (longer than animal rennet).
Cut curd gently into large pieces.
Ladle into small round molds. Do not press heavily.
Salt surfaces. Flip daily for several days.
Age at 46-50°F, high humidity, minimum 60 days.
Cheese should develop soft, oozing interior with firm rind.

notes: Cardoon thistle creates unique bitter, vegetal flavor
Serve by cutting top off and scooping interior
Cannot be imported to USA (raw milk, young aging)

recipes.title: Zamorano (Castile Sheep Cheese)
recipes.description: Hard, intensely flavored cheese similar to Manchego but sharper. Made from Churra and Castellana sheep.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut into very small curds. Stir and heat to 104°F.
Press firmly at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine 48 hours.
Age 6-12 months, coating with olive oil.

notes: Sharper and more intense than Manchego
Traditional zigzag pattern pressed into rind

recipes.title: Ossau-Iraty (French Basque Cheese)
recipes.description: Smooth, firm cheese with sweet, nutty, grassy notes. Made from Basco-Béarnaise and Manech sheep.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces.
Heat slowly to 104°F, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 24-48 hours depending on size.
Age 3-6 months, brushing rind periodically.

notes: Flavor is milder and sweeter than Spanish Basque cheeses

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Emmental/Swiss
recipes.source_note: Classic Swiss cheese adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Large-holed Swiss cheese made with sheep's milk. Nutty and sweet with characteristic eyes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter and P. shermanii. Ripen 15 min.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces.
Heat to 125°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 125°F for 30 minutes.
Press at 30 lbs increasing to 60 lbs over 24 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Age at 55°F for 2 weeks, then 68-72°F for 3-4 weeks for eye development.
Move to 45°F for remaining 3-4 months.

notes: Warm aging period creates the characteristic holes
P. shermanii bacteria produce CO2 that forms eyes
Sheep milk creates richer, more complex Swiss

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Parmesan-Style (Pecorino Aged)
recipes.source_note: Long-aged grating cheese, sheep milk version
recipes.description: Hard, crystalline grating cheese aged 12-24 months. Intensely flavored with complex umami notes.

instructions.text: Skim cream from evening milk. Combine with morning milk.
Heat to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 15 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 15-20 minutes until firm.
Cut into tiny pieces (smaller than rice grains).
Heat to 131°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Let curds settle and mat on bottom.
Press firmly at 50-60 lbs for 24 hours, flipping several times.
Brine 3 weeks, turning daily.
Age 12-24 months at 55°F, turning and brushing weekly.

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Monterey Jack
recipes.source_note: American original adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, creamy, excellent melting cheese. Sheep's milk adds subtle richness to this versatile cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F. Add starter, ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Heat slowly to 102°F over 40 minutes.
Drain whey. Stir curds to dry slightly.
Add salt, mix. Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour, then 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry, wax or vacuum seal. Age 1-3 months.

notes: Add jalapeños for Pepper Jack variant

recipes.title: Pecorino Sardo (Sardinian Sheep Cheese)
recipes.description: Sardinia's signature cheese - firm, nutty, slightly sweet with grassy undertones.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into small pieces (pea-sized).
Cook at 104°F for 15 minutes, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 12-24 hours.
Age: Dolce 1-2 months, Maturo 4-8 months.

recipes.title: Graviera (Greek Gruyère-Style)
recipes.source_note: Greece's second most popular cheese after feta
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty Greek cheese similar to Gruyère. Often served fried as saganaki.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into small pieces.
Heat to 122°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Press at 30 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine 24-48 hours.
Age 3-5 months minimum.

recipes.title: Kefalotiri (Greek Hard Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Greek grating and frying cheese
recipes.description: Very hard, salty Greek cheese. Traditional saganaki cheese when fried.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 40 minutes.
Cut curd very small (rice-grain sized).
Heat to 122°F, stirring constantly.
Press firmly at 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Dry salt for several days, then brine.
Age minimum 3 months, up to 1 year.

notes: Very salty - used for grating and frying

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Muenster
recipes.source_note: Traditional Muenster adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, smooth cheese with orange washed rind. Sheep's milk adds richness to this pungent cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Heat to 100°F over 30 minutes.
Drain and lightly press for 6-8 hours.
Brine 4 hours.
Age at 55°F, 95% humidity. Wash with brine every 2-3 days.
Ready in 3-8 weeks when orange rind develops.

notes: Washing develops the orange rind and pungent aroma
American Muenster is milder than French original

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Taleggio-Style
recipes.source_note: Italian Taleggio adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, washed-rind cheese with meaty, tangy flavor. Sheep's milk creates even richer version.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Let settle 10 minutes. Ladle into square molds.
Flip frequently for 24 hours. Do not press.
Salt all surfaces.
Age at 50°F, high humidity. Wash with brine weekly.
Ready in 6-10 weeks when soft throughout.

notes: Rind should be orange-pink and sticky
Interior should be gooey when ripe

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Reblochon-Style
recipes.source_note: French Alpine Reblochon adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, nutty, washed-rind cheese from Savoie region. Traditional for tartiflette.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Gently stir 5 minutes. Ladle into small round molds.
Flip several times over 6 hours.
Salt and begin washing.
Age 4-6 weeks at 55°F, washing every few days.

notes: Interior should be supple, not runny

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Limburger
recipes.source_note: Classic Limburger adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Notoriously pungent washed-rind cheese. Strong aroma with surprisingly mild, creamy flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 1 hour.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Let rest 10 minutes. Gently stir, drain.
Pack into brick molds. Flip every 15 min for 2 hours.
Brine 12 hours.
Age at 55°F, high humidity. Wash with brine 2x weekly.
Ready in 2-3 months when soft and pungent.

notes: Famous for strong smell, but flavor is mild and creamy
Rind becomes very sticky and smelly

recipes.title: Argentine Magnasco Edam
recipes.source_note: Argentine adaptation of Dutch Edam, dryer and harder than the original. Uses washed-curd method.
recipes.description: Argentina's distinctive Edam cheese, developed by Italian immigrants. Dryer and sharper than Dutch Edam, excellent with crackers and red wine.

ingredients.prep_note: if using pasteurized milk, diluted in 1/4 cup water

instructions.text: Warm milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and calcium chloride if using. Stir thoroughly.
Allow milk to ripen for 30 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet using up-and-down motions. Let set for 30 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 93°F (34°C) over 20 minutes, stirring gently and regularly.
Rest curds at 93°F for 10 minutes.
Drain whey, reserving it. This is the washed-curd method unique to Dutch-style cheeses.
Add warm water (111°F/44°C) equal to whey removed. Stir gently for 1 minute, then rest 10 minutes.
Line mold with cheesecloth. Ladle curds into mold. Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour.
Heat reserved whey to 122°F (50°C). Remove cheese from mold and submerge in hot whey for 20 minutes.
Return to mold with fresh cheesecloth. Press at 40 lbs for 6 hours.
Make saturated brine (2 lbs salt per gallon water). Brine cheese for 12 hours, turning regularly.
Air dry at cool room temperature for 5-7 days, turning daily until rind forms.
Coat with red cheese wax when fully dry.
Age at 52-56°F (11-13°C) and 80-85% humidity for minimum 3 months. For Argentine-style sharpness, age 6+ months.

notes: Argentine Edam is aged longer than Dutch for a dryer, sharper result
The washed-curd method produces a sweeter, milder base that intensifies with aging
Traditional red wax coating is iconic
Magnasco is Argentina's oldest dairy, founded 155+ years ago by Italian immigrants

recipes.title: Argentine Provoleta
recipes.source_note: Argentine pasta filata cheese created by Italian immigrants in the 1940s, designed specifically for grilling.
recipes.description: Argentina's grilling cheese, similar to Italian Provolone but formulated to hold its shape on the grill. Essential for asado.

ingredients.prep_note: dissolved in 1/4 cup cool water, set 20 min

instructions.text: Heat milk to 97°F (36°C). Add thermophilic culture, lipase, and calcium chloride. Mix well using up-and-down motions for 1 minute.
Ripen for 30 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently. Let set 30-45 minutes until firm curd forms.
Cut curds into 3/4-inch pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 116°F (47°C) over 45 minutes, stirring gently to prevent matting.
Continue stirring until curds shrink to rice-grain size and feel springy.
Drain whey. Keep curds warm at 100°F (38°C) for 2-3 hours, turning occasionally, until pH reaches 5.2.
Test for stretch: Place small piece of curd in 170°F (77°C) water. If it stretches smoothly without breaking, proceed.
Heat water or whey to 170°F (77°C). Submerge curds and knead/stretch until smooth and elastic, about 5-10 minutes.
Form into 4-6 inch diameter discs, about 1 inch thick (ideal for grilling). Work quickly before cheese cools.
Plunge formed cheese into ice water bath for 15 minutes to set shape.
Make saturated brine. Brine cheese for 2 hours per pound.
Pat dry and age at 55-60°F (13-16°C) and 80% humidity.
For mild provoleta (dolce), age 2 months. For sharp (piccante), age 6+ months.

notes: The stretch test is critical - curds must reach pH 5.2 for proper stretching
Provoleta was invented specifically for the Argentine asado tradition
Unlike Mozzarella, Provoleta has lower moisture (45%) so it holds shape when grilled
Lipase provides the characteristic piquant flavor

recipes.title: Argentine Reggianito
recipes.source_note: Argentina's interpretation of Parmigiano-Reggiano, developed by Italian immigrants. Aged 5-6 months vs 12-24 months for true Parmigiano.
recipes.description: Argentina's most important hard grating cheese, similar to Parmigiano-Reggiano but smaller wheels and shorter aging. Grainy texture perfect for pasta.

ingredients.prep_note: blend of 1 gal skim + 1 gal whole, or 2% milk
dissolved in 1/4 cup cool water, set 20 min

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture, lipase, and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-45 minutes until firm curd with clean break.
Cut curds very small, to rice-grain size (1/8 inch). This creates the granular texture.
Let curds rest 5 minutes after cutting.
Begin heating slowly to 124°F (51°C) over ONE HOUR, stirring constantly. Do not rush this step.
Continue stirring at 124°F for 30 minutes. Curds should be very small and firm.
Let curds settle to bottom for 5 minutes.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold while still very hot.
Press at 25 lbs for 30 minutes. Remove, flip, redress.
Press at 50 lbs for 12 hours, flipping every few hours.
Make saturated brine. Brine for 18-24 hours, flipping halfway.
Air dry for 3 days at room temperature, turning daily.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) and 80-85% humidity. Turn daily for first 2 weeks, then weekly.
For Reggianito character, age 10-14 months minimum. Rub with olive oil monthly to prevent cracking.

notes: Reggianito means 'Little Reggiano' - made in smaller 15 lb wheels vs 80 lb Parmigiano wheels
The very small curd cut is essential for the granular 'grana' texture
Unlike true Parmigiano, Reggianito does not form salt crystals
Argentina's most exported cheese, credited with pushing Italy to seek PDO protection for Parmigiano-Reggiano

recipes.title: Argentine Sardo
recipes.source_note: Argentina's cow's milk version of Italian Pecorino Sardo. Sharp and salty, perfect for grating.
recipes.description: Argentine grating cheese similar to Pecorino Romano but made with cow's milk instead of sheep's milk. Sharp, salty, and excellent over pasta.

ingredients.prep_note: or blend with 1 gal 1% + 1 gal whole for lower fat
dissolved in 1/4 cup cool water - essential for sharp flavor

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture, lipase, and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 60 minutes at temperature. The longer ripening develops more acid.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-45 minutes until soft curd forms.
Cut curds very small, to rice-grain size (1/8 inch).
Rest 10 minutes after cutting.
Slowly heat curds to 117°F (47°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring at temperature until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 8 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip and redress.
Increase weight gradually over 5-6 hours to 15 lbs, flipping every 30-60 minutes.
Maintain curds at 85-93°F during pressing for proper acid development.
After pressing, let sit overnight at room temperature.
Dry salt all surfaces heavily for several days, or brine for 24 hours in saturated brine.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and 85% humidity. Turn daily for first 2 weeks.
After 2 months, rub periodically with olive oil. Age minimum 10 months for proper sharpness.

notes: Lipase is essential for the sharp, piquant flavor characteristic of Romano-style cheeses
Cow's milk produces a creamy yellow color vs the snow white of true Pecorino
Sardo is saltier than Reggianito - traditionally used as a preservative
Can substitute for Pecorino Romano in any recipe

recipes.title: Australian Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Traditional English-style cheddar as made in Australia and New Zealand. Uses the cheddaring process.
recipes.description: Classic cheddar cheese using the traditional cheddaring method. Firm texture with nutty, tangy flavor that sharpens with age.

ingredients.item: cheese wax or lard and cheesecloth

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes until firm curd with clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 102°F for 30 minutes, stirring to prevent matting.
Drain whey completely. This begins the cheddaring process.
Cut curd mass into 4 blocks. Stack blocks on each other in the warm pot.
Keep at 102°F. Flip and restack blocks every 15 minutes for 2 hours. Curds will become shiny and chicken breast-like in texture.
Mill the cheddared curds into thumb-sized pieces. Mix in salt evenly.
Pack salted curds into cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 20 lbs for 1 hour. Flip, redress, press at 40 lbs for 4-6 hours.
Flip again, press at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Remove from mold. Air dry 2-3 days until surface is dry to touch.
Coat with wax or bandage with lard-soaked cheesecloth.
Age at 52-56°F (11-13°C) and 80-85% humidity. Mild: 3 months. Sharp: 9-12 months. Extra sharp: 18-24 months.

notes: The cheddaring process - stacking and flipping curd blocks - is what defines true cheddar
Curds should elongate and become smooth during cheddaring
Traditional cloth-bound cheddar develops complex flavors; waxed cheddar is more consistent
Australia produces excellent aged cheddars rivaling English originals

recipes.title: Roaring Forties Blue
recipes.source_note: Uniquely creamy Australian blue cheese made exclusively by King Island Dairy in Tasmania.
recipes.description: Exceptionally creamy blue cheese with mild, sweet flavor. Named after the fierce winds that sweep King Island.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 86°F (30°C).
Add mesophilic culture and dissolved P. roqueforti. Stir well.
Add calcium chloride if using. Ripen 60 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 60-90 minutes until soft curd forms.
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Handle very gently - blue cheese curds are delicate.
Let curds rest 10 minutes. Do not heat or stir.
Gently ladle curds into colander lined with cheesecloth. Drain 30 minutes.
Sprinkle salt over curds and gently mix.
Transfer to open-bottom blue cheese mold. Do not press - just let gravity drain.
Flip every 15-30 minutes for first 6 hours, then twice daily for 2-3 days.
Remove from mold. Rub additional salt on surface.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) and 90-95% humidity for 1 week.
Pierce cheese with sterile needle, creating channels throughout. This allows oxygen in for blue development.
Continue aging, turning daily. Blue veins should appear within 2-3 weeks.
When sufficient blue develops (4-6 weeks), wrap in foil to stop further development.
Age wrapped for 2 more weeks. Total: 6-8 weeks minimum.

notes: Extra cream creates the signature super-creamy texture
The Roaring Forties are fierce westerly winds between 40-50° south latitude
King Island's unique terroir comes from cows grazing on wind-swept pastures
Piercing is essential - blue mold needs oxygen to develop

recipes.title: Chimay Trappiste with Beer
recipes.source_note: Famous Belgian monastery cheese washed with Chimay beer. Made by Trappist monks since 1876.
recipes.description: Springy-textured washed-rind cheese with meaty flavor. Rind is washed with Chimay Trappist beer during aging.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add calcium chloride and diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature for 30 minutes, continuing to stir.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip, redress.
Press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip again.
Press at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine in saturated solution for 8 hours, flipping halfway.
Place in aging cave at 55°F (13°C) and 90-95% humidity.
After 2 days, begin washing rind every 2-3 days with beer-brine mixture (1 part beer to 1 part light brine).
Rind will develop orange-pink color from B. linens over several weeks.
Continue washing and aging for 6-8 weeks total.
Cheese is ready when rind is fully developed and interior is supple but not runny.

notes: Trappist monks developed this style at Chimay Abbey in Belgium
The beer wash contributes complex flavors and promotes B. linens growth
Authentic Chimay cheese carries the ATP (Authentic Trappist Product) label
Semi-soft texture should be springy, with aromatic rind and meaty flavor

recipes.title: Austrian Moosbacher
recipes.source_note: Unique Austrian cheese combining Emmental-style eyes with washed-rind treatment. Named after a Styrian farmer.
recipes.description: The only cheese with both large eyes (like Swiss) and a washed rind. Sweet, fruity, with hints of toasted hazelnuts.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add all cultures (thermophilic, propionic, and B. linens). Stir well.
Add calcium chloride. Ripen for 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch pieces (small for proper eye development).
Let rest 5 minutes. Begin stirring gently.
Slowly heat to 120°F (49°C) over 45 minutes, stirring continuously.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes. Curds should be firm and springy.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to large mold lined with cheesecloth.
Press at 15 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip, redress.
Press at 30 lbs for 6 hours, flipping every 2 hours.
Press at 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 18-24 hours in saturated brine.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and high humidity for 2 weeks, washing with brine every 2-3 days.
Move to warm room 68-72°F (20-22°C) for 2-3 weeks to develop eyes. Propionic bacteria become active.
When eyes have formed, return to 55°F. Continue washing rind with brine.
Age 3-4 months total. Rind should be orange-brown, interior should have scattered large eyes.

notes: Moosbacher is unique - the only cheese with both eyes AND washed rind
The dual-ripening process requires careful temperature management
Named after one of the Styrian farmers who supply milk for this cheese
Flavor described as cross between Gouda and Appenzeller

recipes.title: Canadian Oka
recipes.source_note: Made in Quebec since 1893, first created by Trappist monks who emigrated from France.
recipes.description: Semi-soft washed-rind cheese with piquant flavor. Quebec's most famous cheese, originally from Port-du-Salut tradition.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Stir well.
Add calcium chloride. Ripen for 60 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd with clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 96°F (36°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature for 30 minutes, continuing to stir.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 8 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip and redress.
Press at 15 lbs for 2 hours. Flip again.
Press at 25 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated solution.
Place in aging cave at 55°F (13°C) and 90-95% humidity.
Wash rind with light brine every 2-3 days for first 3 weeks.
Rind will develop orange color from B. linens.
Age 6-8 weeks total. Interior should be pale yellow and slightly aromatic.
Ready when rind is fully developed and cheese has slight piquant taste.

notes: Trappist monks brought Port-du-Salut recipe from France to Quebec
Oka was Canada's first artisan cheese
Now made commercially but traditional methods still used by small producers
Semi-soft texture with piquant, slightly aromatic flavor

recipes.title: Eastern European Kurpianka
recipes.source_note: Salami-shaped Polish cheese, often smoked. Traditional snacking cheese from the Kurpie region.
recipes.description: Cylindrical smoked cheese with firm texture. Popular as a snacking cheese in Poland and Eastern Europe.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature for 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Mix salt into curds.
Pack curds into cylindrical salami-shaped molds.
Press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip and redress.
Press at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Remove from mold. Air dry for 2-3 days until surface is dry.
Cold smoke at 70-80°F (21-27°C) for 4-8 hours, or until golden brown.
Rest overnight after smoking.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) for 2-4 weeks.
Cheese can be eaten young (2 weeks) or aged longer for stronger flavor.

notes: Kurpianka comes from the Kurpie forest region of Poland
The salami shape is traditional and practical for slicing
Excellent paired with Polish mustard and dark bread

recipes.title: Eastern European Podlaski
recipes.source_note: Flavorful yellow cheese from the Podlasie region of Poland. Good for melting or snacking.
recipes.description: Semi-hard Polish cheese with rich yellow color and full flavor. Excellent for melting in dishes or eating as a snack.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F (31°C). Add mesophilic culture, annatto if using, and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 3/8-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature for 30 minutes, stirring to keep curds separated.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour. Flip and redress.
Press at 30 lbs for 6 hours. Flip again.
Press at 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 12-18 hours in saturated brine.
Air dry for 3-5 days at cool room temperature.
Wax or vacuum seal for aging.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) for 2-3 months minimum.

notes: Podlasie is a region in northeastern Poland known for dairy
Annatto gives the traditional golden-yellow color
Excellent melting properties make it great for cooking
Pairs well with Polish kielbasa and rye bread

recipes.title: Belgian Capra (Fresh Goat Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Fresh Belgian goat cheese (chèvre) available plain or flavored with honey or herbs.
recipes.description: Soft, creamy fresh goat cheese with tangy flavor. Can be enjoyed plain or with honey, herbs, or other flavorings.

instructions.text: Heat goat's milk to 72°F (22°C) - just slightly warm.
Add mesophilic culture. Stir gently.
Add diluted rennet. Stir briefly.
Cover and let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours until curd forms a solid mass.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Tie cheesecloth corners and hang to drain for 6-12 hours.
Transfer drained cheese to bowl. Mix in salt.
For flavored versions, fold in honey, fresh herbs, cracked pepper, or other seasonings.
Shape into logs, balls, or pack into containers.
Refrigerate. Best consumed within 1-2 weeks.

notes: Very little rennet is used - acid does most of the work
Fresh chèvre is meant to be eaten young
Popular flavorings include herbs de Provence, honey, and cracked pepper

recipes.title: Belgian Passendale
recipes.source_note: Sweet semi-soft Belgian cheese with many small holes. Named after the village of Passendale.
recipes.description: Mild, sweet semi-soft cheese with characteristic small holes throughout. Buttery flavor with hints of grass.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture and calcium chloride. Stir well.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature 20 minutes. Curds should be springy.
Drain whey. Transfer curds to mold.
Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour. Flip, redress.
Press at 25 lbs for 6 hours. Flip.
Press at 35 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated solution.
Air dry for 2-3 days.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and 85% humidity for 4-6 weeks.
Small eyes will develop naturally during aging.

notes: Named after Passendale village in West Flanders
Distinctive round loaf shape with domed top
The many small holes develop naturally from mesophilic culture
Mild enough for children, flavorful enough for adults

recipes.title: Belgian Wynendale
recipes.source_note: Decidedly spicy, ultra-creamy Belgian cheese with pronounced aroma.
recipes.description: Rich, creamy Belgian cheese with spicy kick and strong aroma. Triple-cream style with assertive flavor.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 72°F (22°C).
Add all cultures (mesophilic, P. candidum, Geotrichum). Stir gently.
Add calcium chloride and diluted rennet.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
Curd should be thick and slightly acidic. Ladle gently into molds.
Let drain at room temperature for 24 hours, flipping 2-3 times.
Remove from molds. Salt all surfaces lightly.
Place on mat in ripening container.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and 90-95% humidity.
White mold will develop over first week. Turn daily.
Ready in 3-4 weeks when rind is fully developed and interior is creamy.

notes: Triple-cream cheese with at least 75% butterfat in dry matter
The spicy notes develop with age
Aroma is pronounced but flavor is rich and balanced

recipes.title: Swiss-Style Emmental
recipes.source_note: The original 'Swiss cheese' with distinctive large eyes. Made in Switzerland, Belgium, Austria, and beyond.
recipes.description: Classic Swiss cheese with large characteristic holes (eyes). Nutty, slightly sweet flavor. Essential for fondue.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture and propionic bacteria. Stir well.
Add calcium chloride. Ripen for 10 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch pieces - very small for proper texture.
Let rest 5 minutes. Begin stirring gently.
Slowly heat to 120-125°F (49-52°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at temperature for 30-45 minutes. Curds should be firm and springy.
Drain whey. Transfer curds quickly to large mold - keep them hot.
Press at 20 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip, redress.
Press at 40 lbs for 6 hours, flipping every 2 hours.
Press at 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine for 24-48 hours in saturated brine (longer for larger wheels).
Age at 55°F (13°C) for 2 weeks, turning daily.
Move to warm room 68-74°F (20-23°C) for 3-4 weeks. This activates propionic bacteria to form eyes.
Watch for slight bulging as eyes form. Tap cheese - should sound hollow.
Return to 55°F. Age 4-6 months total, turning weekly.

notes: Propionic bacteria produce CO2 which forms the characteristic eyes
The warm room stage is critical - too cold and eyes won't form
Traditional wheels are 200+ lbs, but home batches work well smaller
Used in Swiss fondue along with Gruyère

recipes.title: Swiss-Style Gruyère
recipes.source_note: Famous Alpine cheese from Switzerland, also made in Belgium. Smaller holes than Emmental.
recipes.description: Complex, nutty Alpine cheese with small scattered eyes. Excellent melting cheese, essential for fondue and gratins.

ingredients.prep_note: less than Emmental for smaller eyes

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add thermophilic culture and propionic bacteria. Stir well.
Add calcium chloride. Ripen for 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch pieces.
Let rest 5 minutes. Stir gently.
Slowly heat to 120°F (49°C) over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes. Curds should be very firm.
Drain whey. Keep curds hot as you transfer to mold.
Press at 25 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip.
Press at 50 lbs for 6 hours, flipping every 2 hours.
Press at 60 lbs for 18 hours.
Brine for 24-48 hours in saturated brine.
Age at 55°F (13°C) for 3 weeks, washing with brine every few days.
Move to warm room 65°F (18°C) for 2-3 weeks for eye development.
Return to cool aging. Continue washing rind.
Age minimum 5 months. Reserve Gruyère ages 10-12 months.

notes: Gruyère has smaller, fewer eyes than Emmental
The washed rind contributes to flavor complexity
PDO protected in Switzerland - elsewhere called 'Gruyère-style'
One of the world's great melting cheeses

recipes.title: English Caerphilly
recipes.source_note: Originally from Wales, now mostly made in England. White cheese with chalky to creamy texture.
recipes.description: Simple white cheese with lemony tang. Young Caerphilly is chalky; aged versions become creamy. Quick to make.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add mesophilic culture and calcium chloride. Stir.
Ripen for 45 minutes at temperature.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir curds for 10 minutes. Do not heat.
Let curds settle. Drain off whey to curd level.
Stir curds gently. Let rest 10 minutes. Repeat 2-3 times over 30 minutes.
Drain remaining whey. Mix in salt.
Transfer curds to cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes. Flip.
Press at 20 lbs for 2 hours. Flip.
Press at 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Remove and air dry for 2-3 days until surface is dry.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and 85% humidity. Edible in 2 weeks; fuller flavor at 6-8 weeks.

notes: One of the quickest hard cheeses to make and age
Originally made for Welsh coal miners - high salt content replaced lost minerals
Young = chalky and crumbly; aged = creamy and complex
No cooking step keeps it moist and quick-aging

recipes.title: English Cheshire
recipes.source_note: One of England's oldest cheeses, allegedly invented during the 12th century. Crumbly and slightly salty.
recipes.description: Historic English cheese with crumbly texture. Rich, mellow, slightly salty with excellent aftertaste.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture, annatto if using, and calcium chloride.
Ripen for 60 minutes. Cheshire needs extra acid development.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 60 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curds into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Slowly heat to 94°F (34°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at temperature for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain whey. Let curds mat in pot for 15 minutes.
Cut curd mass into strips. Stack and turn every 15 minutes for 1 hour (mild cheddaring).
Mill curds into walnut-sized pieces. Mix in salt.
Pack into mold. Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour.
Flip, press at 30 lbs for 6 hours.
Flip, press at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Bandage with cloth or wax. Age at 55°F (13°C) for 2-6 months.

notes: Cheshire salt deposits in the region contribute unique minerality
Crumblier than Cheddar due to higher acid and different curd handling
Red Cheshire uses annatto; white Cheshire is natural color
Flavor sharpens and deepens with age

recipes.title: English Stilton (Blue)
recipes.source_note: The 'King of Cheeses' - England's famous blue-veined cheese. PDO protected, made only in specific counties.
recipes.description: Rich, mellow blue cheese with piquant aftertaste. Blue-green veins through creamy ivory paste. Pairs with Port.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 86°F (30°C).
Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Stir gently.
Add calcium chloride and rennet. Let set 90 minutes until soft curd.
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Handle very gently.
Let rest 10 minutes. Do not stir or heat.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined colander. Drain 30 minutes.
Break curds gently into walnut-sized pieces. Mix in salt.
Transfer to tall cylindrical mold (Stilton's traditional shape). Do not press.
Turn mold daily for 5-6 days. Cheese will compress under own weight.
Remove from mold. Scrape surface smooth.
Age at 55°F (13°C) and 90% humidity for 2-3 weeks.
